To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed system architecture can effectively and efficiently transform a passive interactive CBT system into an active one, that the system is able to generate and execute a large number of tasks to information sources autonomously, and that it is effective and efficient in diagnosing equipment problems.

(1) we propose an active CBR system that uses cases as information tasks to be autonomously performed on multiple information resources; (2) we present a hierarchical planning and execution framework for information gathering tasks; (3) we demonstrate our approach on an equipment diagnosis domain, and show how our system can autonomously diagnose the problem with a piece of equipment.
we propose a system that integrates CBR retrieval, hierarchical query planning, query optimization and query execution.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and evaluation of a CBR system architecture that is able to actively gather information in an intelligent manner, and thus provide an advisor role in a more proactive and efficient fashion.
the design and implementation of a new class of CBR systems which we term autonomous information gathering CBR systems.
the problem of how to make a CBR system more autonomous in the information gathering phase.

this paper presents a novel approach to CBR system development that can be applied to a variety of domains.
our work is an important contribution to the CBR field in that it provides a new perspective on CBR systems and demonstrates how CBR systems can be used in a novel and effective way.
the system is a successful demonstration of the feasibility of the approach and the potential for its application to a variety of domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a CBR system that can autonomously generate and execute queries for itself.

we have demonstrated that CBR systems are capable of being used in an autonomous, active role in information gathering applications, and the system architecture and algorithm can be applied to other CBR domains.
we have developed a system that can automatically gather information from multiple information sources, and then apply CBR retrieval on the gathered information to make an assessment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CBR system can act as a meta-planner for the information gathering process, which is a useful feature for many real-world applications.
CBR can be used as an information gathering mechanism to support active CBR systems.
the CBR system can act as a knowledge-based information gathering engine that autonomously performs information tasks on multiple information sources.
